ra: Cú Chulainn is the central hero of the Ulster Cycle (Kinsella, The Táin).
Conchobar mac Nessa is king of the Ulaid in the Ulster Cycle.
Medb of Connacht is the antagonist-queen of the Táin within the Ulster Cycle.
Fergus mac Róich is a principal figure of the Ulster Cycle and the Táin.
Deirdre is heroine of a remscél of the Táin within the Ulster Cycle.
Scáthach appears in Tochmarc Emire as Cú Chulainn's instructor in the Ulster Cycle.
Emer is Cú Chulainn's wife within the Ulster Cycle.
Fionn mac Cumhaill is the central hero of the Fenian Cycle (Ó hÓgáin).
Oisín, son of Fionn, is namesake of the Ossianic/Fenian Cycle.
Diarmuid Ua Duibhne is a leading fian warrior in the Fenian Cycle.
Gráinne is heroine of the Fenian pursuit-tale Tóraigheacht Dhiarmada agus Ghráinne.
The banshee is a core Irish folklore being (Ó hÓgáin, Lore of Ireland).
The leprechaun is a core Irish folklore being.
The púca is a core Irish folklore being.
The dullahan is a core Irish folklore death-being.
The changeling is a recurrent Irish fairy-belief motif.
The aos sí form the encompassing class of the Irish folklore otherworld beings.
Cú Chulainn is the son (and earthly aspect) of the god Lugh in the Ulster Cycle (Kinsella; Ó hÓgáin).
Cú Chulainn functions as a heroic, euhemerised reflex of the divine Lugh.
Scáthach trains Cú Chulainn in arms and gives him the gáe bolga (Tochmarc Emire).
Emer is the wife of Cú Chulainn (Tochmarc Emire).
Fergus is the lover of Medb during his Connacht exile in the Táin.
Oisín is the son of Fionn mac Cumhaill.
Diarmuid is the foster-son of the god Aengus, who protects him in the pursuit-tale (Ó hÓgáin).
Gráinne elopes with and becomes the partner of Diarmuid.
Fionn pursues Diarmuid and Gráinne after their elopement in the Fenian pursuit-tale.
Partholón's people battle the Fomorians in the Lebor Gabála invasion sequence.
Nemed and his descendants war against the Fomorians in the Lebor Gabála Érenn.
The Sons of Míl defeat the Tuatha Dé Danann and take Ireland in the Lebor Gabála Érenn.
Tuan mac Cairill, the shapeshifting survivor, belongs to the broader Irish legendary/lore stratum; tying him into a hub for connectivity.
Fintan mac Bóchra is the husband of Cesair in the Lebor Gabála Érenn.
Cesair belongs to the invasion-sequence lore; wiring her to the invasion hub for connectivity (note: distinct from the Gaelic Milesians proper, linked only as invasion stratum).
Partholón and Nemed are successive invasion leaders in the same Lebor Gabála sequence; linking the invasion figures for graph connectivity.
Tailtiu is the foster-mother of the god Lugh, whose funeral games became Lughnasa (Ó hÓgáin).
The Fomorian-allied sorceress Carman and her sons are driven off by the Tuatha Dé in the dindshenchas.
The Cailleach and Tailtiu are both sovereignty/landscape goddesses of the Irish countryside; grouped functionally.
Tlachtga and Carman are both eponymous landscape goddesses of Irish assembly-sites in the dindshenchas.
The aos sí are understood in later tradition as the diminished Tuatha Dé Danann withdrawn into the síde (Ó hÓgáin).
The bean sí ('woman of the síde') is a member of the fairy folk.
